item.title: Hasedera: The Flower Temple and Its Grand Stairway — Guide
item.description: Hasedera, in the mountains of eastern Nara near Sakurai, is one of Japan’s great flower temples and the head of the Buzan Shingon school. Its signature is the Noboriro, a magnificent roofed corridor of 399 stone steps that climbs the hillside beneath hanging lanterns to the main hall, which stands on a stilted veranda overlooking the valley in the manner of Kiyomizu-dera. Inside towers a magnificent 10-metre-plus gilded statue of Kannon, the goddess of mercy — one of the largest wooden statues in Japan.
